names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 7 Δεκεμβρίου, «Όσιος Παύλος ο Υποτακτικός», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru’s line for 7 декабря ст. ст., «Павел Послушливый (Повинник), прп.», with the rank word left off. Both epithets are kept because the calendar prints both and the parenthesis is its own, not an abbreviation of one of them; neither word is a rank. The line on the day page itself gives the name in the genitive with the first epithet only.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 7 декабря ст. ст. — «Прп. Павла Послушливого.»

attestations.note: The same man and the same menologion day: this folder's Greek row is already Paul the Obedient, and «Послушливый» is that epithet in Russian. Both books tell the same two things of him — the boiling pitch he stirred with his hand unburned, and the going to Jerusalem, then Cyprus, then the mountain where he died — and this one names the mountain Паригори where the Greek one has Parigoria. The line gives him no year and neither page does; `dates` stays absent.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (2 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Όσιος Παύλος ο Υποτακτικός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page opens by saying that the synaxaria do not record where he came from or where he was a monk, so no origin and no house are drafted. The corpus keeps `paul-the-obedient-of-the-caves`, «Όσιος Παύλος ο Υπάκουος ο ἐν τῷ Σπηλαίῳ», with a venerated Greek row on 10 September; that is a different by-name, a different day and therefore a different commemoration, and nothing on either page joins the two. No year, so no `dates` object. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (2 October 2026).
